t: Client-selected V1 serializer crashes shared broadcast dispatch on binary payloads
d: Uncaught Exception vulnerability in phoenixframework phoenix allows an unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial of service via a client-selected legacy serializer on binary channel broadcasts. When an application broadcasts {:binary, data} payloads on a channel topic, any client that connects without a vsn parameter, or with vsn=1.0.0, and joins that topic makes those broadcasts fail. Phoenix.Channel.Server.send/4 encodes each broadcast with every subscriber's own serializer inside the PubSub dispatch loop, calling fastlane!/1 with no rescue, and the negotiated Phoenix.Socket.V1.JSONSerializer raises Protocol.UndefinedError on a binary payload. Every binary broadcast on the topic then crashes the broadcasting process and skips every subscriber dispatched after the attacker. For broadcasts arriving from other nodes the loop runs in the PubSub adapter worker, whose repeated crashes restart the PubSub supervisor and empty the node's subscription registry while sockets stay connected. This issue affects phoenix: from 1.5.7 before 1.5.16, from 1.6.0-rc.0 before 1.6.18, from 1.7.0-rc.0 before 1.7.25, and from 1.8.0-rc.0 before 1.8.17.

t: kanishka-linux reminiscence Chromium HTML-to-PDF Conversion Pipeline dbaccess.py convert_html_pdf_with_chromium os command injection
d: A vulnerability was identified in kanishka-linux reminiscence 0.3 on Windows. This issue affects the function convert_html_pdf_with_chromium of the file pages/dbaccess.py of the component Chromium HTML-to-PDF Conversion Pipeline. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

t: Unlimited Elements For Elementor <= 2.0.26 - Authenticated (Contributor+) Arbitrary File Read via SVG Icon URL Parameter in get_addon_output_data AJAX Action
d: The Unlimited Elements For Elementor plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Directory Traversal in all versions up to, and including, 2.0.26 via the getFileContentByUrl function. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to read the contents of arbitrary files on the server, which can contain sensitive information. The nonce protecting the get_addon_output_data AJAX endpoint is emitted on the Elementor editor page, which is accessible to Contributors, making the endpoint reachable by any authenticated user at that privilege level or above.

t: Germanized for WooCommerce <= 4.1.8 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Billing First Name via WC Store API / Guest Withdrawal Request
d: The Germanized for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'billing_address.first_name (Store API checkout) → stored on parent order; withdrawal get_first_name() fallback' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.1.8 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The payload is planted via an unauthenticated guest checkout order's billing first name through the WooCommerce Store API, with execution triggered by a subsequent unauthenticated withdrawal request submission whose nonce is publicly available on the /withdraw-from-contract/ page.

t: WP Data Access <= 5.5.92 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via HyperlinkObject Label via Anonymous Registration Form
d: The WP Data Access – App Builder for Tables, Forms, Dashboards, Charts & Maps plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'HyperlinkObject.label (percent-encoded)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.5.92 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires the WordPress site to have a published Anonymous-access Registration Form app configured against a table with a HyperlinkObject column, and a legacy Data Project list using a $$link$$ Dynamic Hyperlink against that same column; given this configuration, any unauthenticated visitor can plant the payload.
r: WP Data Access – App Builder for Tables, Forms, Dashboards, Charts & Maps

t: Stream <= 4.4.0 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via User Display Name
d: The Stream – Activity Log & Audit Trail plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'display_name' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.4.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This is only exploitable on sites with 50 or fewer total users, as above that threshold the user filter uses an AJAX endpoint that returns entity-encoded labels and is not affected.

t: Tutor LMS <= 4.2.0 - Missing Authorization to Authenticated (Subscriber+) Arbitrary Content Deletion via 'question_id' Parameter
d: The Tutor LMS – eLearning and online course solution plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 4.2.0 This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. t: Stream <= 4.5.0 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via BuddyPress Group Name

This requires BuddyPress to be active with its Groups component enabled and default group-creation permissions in place, allowing any logged-in member to create groups.

t: Thim Kit for Elementor <= 1.4.8 - Unauthenticated Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via Comment Content
d: The Thim Kit for Elementor – Pre-built Templates & Widgets for Elementor plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.4.8 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. t: VikBooking Hotel Booking Engine & PMS <= 1.8.20 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'inquiry' Array Key Parameter

t: Simply Schedule Appointments <= 1.6.13.4 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'payment_method' Parameter
d: The Simply Schedule Appointments plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'payment_method' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.6.13.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The stored payload is only rendered when an administrator navigates to the hidden support page (/wp-admin/admin.php?ssa-support-admin=1) and triggers the 'Fix appointment durations' action, a condition reliably engineered by the attacker by smuggling a '+1 day' suffix in the start_date field to create a persistent duration mismatch that routes the malicious booking through the vulnerable echo path. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

t: WP Compress <= 7.26.00 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Read via Path Traversal via 'css' Parameter via Cookie-Planted Boundary Directory
d: The WP Compress – Instant Performance & Speed Optimization plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Directory Traversal in all versions up to, and including, 7.26.00 via the 'css' parameter parameter. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to read the contents of arbitrary files on the server, which can contain sensitive information. Exploiting the file read requires a preparatory unauthenticated request that plants a boundary directory by injecting a path traversal sequence into a cookie listed in WPC_CACHE_COOKIES (such as pll_language, present in the default list), meaning the plugin's cookie-cache feature must be enabled with at least one tracked cookie name configured.
r: WP Compress – Instant Performance & Speed Optimization

t: Hustle <= 7.8.14.4 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Module Import File 'main_content' Parameter
d: The Hustle – Email Marketing, Lead Generation, Optins, Popups plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'import_file' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.8.14.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This requires an administrator to have first delegated the hustle_edit_module capability to a lower-privileged role via the plugin's built-in Permissions screen; without that delegation, the import endpoint rejects non-Administrator users at the capability check.
r: Hustle – Email Marketing, Lead Generation, Optins, Popups

t: WP Fastest Cache <= 1.5.4 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary Directory Deletion via Path Traversal via Permalink Path Traversal in singleDeleteCache / delete_next_prev
d: The WP Fastest Cache – WordPress Cache Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to arbitrary directory deletion due to insufficient file path validation in the singleDeleteCache function in all versions up to, and including, 1.5.4 This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files on the server, which can easily lead to remote code execution when the right file is deleted (such as wp-config.php). Successful exploitation requires either the Custom Permalinks plugin or the GeoDirectory plugin to be co-installed, as these provide the necessary mechanism to write a traversal-bearing permalink value into the database that WP Fastest Cache then consumes without validation.
r: WP Fastest Cache – WordPress Cache Plugin

t: HUSKY <= 1.4.7 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) SQL Injection via 'woof_text' Parameter
d: The HUSKY – Products Filter for WooCommerce Professional plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to time-based SQL Injection via the 'link (inner 'woof_text' query parameter)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.4.7 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database. The exploit requires a valid product_messenger nonce, which is issued by the woof_redraw_woof AJAX endpoint to any visitor when the shortcode's by_only attribute is set — an attribute that can itself be forced via the attacker-controlled woof_shortcode request parameter, making the nonce trivially obtainable by any logged-in user.
r: HUSKY – Products Filter for WooCommerce Professional. MCP is onboard

t: VikBooking Hotel Booking Engine & PMS <= 1.8.20 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'vbf<field_id>' Custom Booking Field Parameters

t: Tutor LMS <= 4.2.0 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Profile Bio

t: WPC Frequently Bought Together for WooCommerce <= 8.0.2 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'variation' Parameter

r: WPC Frequently Bought Together for WooCommerce

t: Unbounce Landing Pages <= 1.1.6 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via REQUEST_URI via Proxy Error Handling
d: The Unbounce Landing Pages plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting in versions up to, and including, 1.1.6. This is due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping on the proxy error message that is persisted to the 'ub-proxy-error-message' option: unauthenticated attacker-controlled REQUEST_URI data is concatenated into the error string in UBHTTP::stream_request_curl()/stream_request_wp_remote() and stored via update_option(), then later echoed inside a <textarea> on the Unbounce Pages Diagnostics admin page without any escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user (an administrator viewing the Diagnostics screen) accesses an injected page.

t: Bytebase DBHub Read Only Mode allowed-keywords.ts escapeHatchFunctionKeywords incomplete blacklist
d: A security vulnerability has been detected in Bytebase DBHub up to 2.0.0. t: MaysWind AriaNg-Native IPC main-process.js shell.openPath input validation
d: A vulnerability was determined in MaysWind AriaNg-Native up to 1.3.14. Affected by this issue is the function shell.openPath of the file main/ipc/main-process.js of the component IPC Handler. Patch name: ac5a4bcf102f605b160f19fcc9fbaec67f9596d7. You should upgrade the affected component.

t: SiteOrigin CSS <= 1.6.9 - Unauthenticated Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via 'class' Attribute of Stored Content via Visual Inspector
d: The SiteOrigin CSS plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'class' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.6.9 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires a Contributor-level or higher attacker to store a crafted class attribute value in a post, which then fires when a user with the edit_theme_options capability opens the Visual Inspector on the affected post and clicks anywhere in the preview iframe. Exploitation by unauthenticated attackers requires that a third-party plugin providing wp_kses_post()-filtered unauthenticated front-end submission is installed and configured, and a moderator approves the submission. On a default installation, where that is not configured, the vulnerability requires attackers with contributor-level access and above.

t: Redux Framework <= 4.5.17 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Color Field Validator Warning Message
d: The Redux Framework plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the '<opt_name>[<color-field-id>]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.5.17 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The wp_kses_post() sanitization applied via Redux_Helpers::sanitize_array() is bypassed — not broken — because an <a class="thickbox" title="&lt;img onerror=...&gt;"> payload uses only kses-allowed tags and attributes, with the entity-encoded onerror handler surviving storage as inert text that the browser decodes when WordPress core's thickbox.js reads the title attribute and writes it into the modal as HTML. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

t: ShortPixel Image Optimizer <= 6.6.1 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Comment Content via CDN URL Rewriter
d: The ShortPixel Image Optimizer – Optimize Images, Convert WebP & AVIF plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 6.6.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires the administrator to have enabled the 'Deliver WebP/AVIF images using the ShortPixel CDN' (useCDN) option, after which any unauthenticated visitor can submit a comment containing a crafted url() payload inside an allowed HTML construct such as <acronym title="...">, which WordPress comment kses preserves on save; the dangerous attribute-boundary breakout occurs only at render time inside the ob_start output-buffer rewriter, where kses does not apply.
r: ShortPixel Image Optimizer – Optimize Images, Convert WebP & AVIF

t: SchemaEngine AI <= 3.1.3 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Comment Content via WebPage JSON-LD Description
d: The SchemaEngine AI – AI Schema Markup, Reviews & Rich Snippets for SEO plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Comment Content via WebPage JSON-LD Description in all versions up to, and including, 3.1.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. r: SchemaEngine AI – AI Schema Markup, Reviews & Rich Snippets for SEO

t: Product Import Export for WooCommerce <= 2.6.9 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Product Review Import Placeholder Re-expansion
d: The Product Import Export for WooCommerce – CSV Product Importer & Exporter plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'author (initial store via wp-comments-post.php) / CSV cell on import' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.6.9 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The exploit requires an administrator to approve the attacker's review, then export and re-import it using the plugin's default column mapping, with the import taking the INSERT branch — which occurs automatically on any site whose database table prefix is not the literal 'wp_', when the CSV has no comment_ID mapping, or when the original review has been trashed. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.
r: Product Import Export for WooCommerce – CSV Product Importer & Exporter

t: Forminator Forms <= 1.58.4 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Rich-Text Textarea Save-and-Continue Draft
d: The Forminator Forms – Contact Form, Payment Form & Custom Form Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'textarea-N (rich-text draft value, saved as Save-and-Continue draft meta)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.58.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires the targeted form to have a Rich-Text Textarea field with Save-and-Continue enabled and public submission permissions — once a crafted draft is saved, the payload executes whenever any user, including an administrator, resumes the draft or opens the Draft ID link from the Forminator Submissions screen.
r: Forminator Forms – Contact Form, Payment Form & Custom Form Builder

t: Organize Media Folder <= 2.00 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via EXIF 'DateTimeOriginal' Metadata
d: The Organize Media Folder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'EXIF.DateTimeOriginal' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.00 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This bypass of wp_filter_post_kses means the injected payload survives regardless of the uploader's unfiltered_html capability; Subscriber-level access becomes sufficient when a front-end attachment-upload integration such as bbPress with forumAttachments is active, and exploitation requires no special configuration because the %created_timestamp% placeholder is included in the caption template by default. Exploitation by attackers with subscriber-level access and above requires that bbPress and gd-bbpress-attachments (forumAttachments) are installed and configured so that Subscribers/Participants can post attachments through a frontend forum form. On a default installation, where that is not configured, the vulnerability requires attackers with author-level access and above.

t: Forminator Forms <= 1.58.4 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Uploaded .rtx File
d: The Forminator Forms – Contact Form, Payment Form & Custom Form Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'upload-1 (the File Upload field's element_id)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.58.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. d: The Admin Columns plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'url' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.1.8 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. t: BlockStrap Page Builder <= 0.1.65 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Comment Content
d: The BlockStrap Page Builder – Bootstrap Blocks plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 0.1.65 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. t: Admin Columns <= 7.1.7 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'User-Agent' Header via comment_agent
d: The Admin Columns plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'HTTP_USER_AGENT' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.1.7 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The kses sanitization pass in classes/Sanitize/Kses.php uses wp_kses_allowed_html('post') augmented with iframe[src] and the data: protocol; because wp_kses_attr_check accepts any data-* attribute on any allowed tag without inspecting its value, a payload embedded inside a data-ac-tip attribute survives intact and is subsequently assigned to innerHTML by assets/js/table.js, bypassing the apparent mitigation entirely.

t: Shortcodes Ultimate <= 7.9.1 - Unauthenticated Local File Inclusion via 'Host' Header via %CURRENT_URL% in [su_qrcode]
d: The Shortcodes Ultimate plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Local File Inclusion in versions up to, and including, 7.9.1 This is due to su_get_current_url() interpolating the raw Host request header into the authority portion of a URL that is then passed to esc_url() — which by design preserves '[' and ']' inside the authority so IPv6 literal hosts remain valid — and the [su_qrcode] shortcode substituting that value into its data attribute (the documented %CURRENT_URL% token) before feeding it to do_shortcode(). This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to include arbitrary PHP files that reside within the active theme's root directory (bounded because '/' inside an attribute value terminates parse_url()'s host and is then percent-encoded and stripped), and — when the shipped-default 'Unsafe features' option remains on — to read arbitrary post meta of any post, on any front-end page that renders [su_qrcode data="%CURRENT_URL%"].

t: Photo Gallery, Sliders, Proofing and Themes <= 4.5.6 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Comment Link via Thickbox Lightbox 'all_images' Context
d: The Photo Gallery, Sliders, Proofing and Themes – NextGEN Gallery plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.5.6 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This requires the site administrator to have configured the Thickbox lightbox effect with the "Try to apply to all images" context (thumbEffectContext=all_images), and exploitation additionally depends on an administrator approving the attacker's initial comment so that subsequent comments from that author are auto-approved.
r: Photo Gallery, Sliders, Proofing and Themes – NextGEN Gallery

d: The WPBot – AI ChatBot for WordPress & Growth Suite: SEO, AI Writer, Email Marketing, Social Media plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'text' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 9.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. d: The MetForm – Contact Form, Survey, Quiz, Conditional Forms, Form Templates & Custom Form Builder for Elementor plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'mf-te (the form-builder-chosen name of the Text Editor field)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.3.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. t: Coupon Creator <= 3.6.5 - Authenticated (Contributor+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'cctor_expiration' Post Meta
d: The Coupon Creator plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'metavalue (with metakeyinput=cctor_expiration)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.6.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The exploit is possible because the cctor_coupon post type advertises 'custom-fields' support, enabling WordPress core's Custom Fields metabox for Contributors, and the unregistered cctor_expiration meta key causes sanitize_meta() to be a no-op, allowing raw HTML to be stored verbatim in the database via a single AJAX request.

t: Fastcache by Host.it <= 1.7.14 - Reflected Cross-Site Scripting via 's' Parameter
d: The Fastcache by Host.it plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Reflected Cross-Site Scripting via the 's' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.7.14 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that execute if they can successfully trick a user into performing an action such as clicking on a link. This code path is only reachable when both the Light Images feature and the DOMDocument entity-decode branch are enabled (lightimgs_status = 1 and img_processing_entity_decode = 1), which reflect the default plugin configuration.

t: Quay: quay: webhook notifications allow ssrf via incomplete hostname validation
d: A flaw was found in Quay. Insufficient validation of repository notification webhook URLs allows an authenticated administrator to trigger Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF). By specifying an internal URL or a redirect to an internal destination, an attacker can force the Quay worker to issue unauthorized HTTP requests to internal network locations and cloud metadata services.

t: rtMedia for WordPress, BuddyPress and bbPress <= 4.7.18 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via 'media_title' Parameter
d: The rtMedia for WordPress, BuddyPress and bbPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'media_title' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.7.18 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The vulnerability is only triggerable via the Backbone.js-rendered "Load More" pagination path; the server-side PHP gallery rendering correctly escapes media_title with esc_attr() and is not affected.
r: rtMedia for WordPress, BuddyPress and bbPress

t: WP Import Export Lite <= 3.9.32 - Unauthenticated Stored Code Execution via Placeholder Substitution in Imported Comment Content
d: The WP Import Export Lite plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Limited Code Injection in all versions up to, and including, 3.9.32 via the 'comment' parameter. This is due to a two-stage shortcode check that evaluates the raw mapping placeholder before data substitution, causing the neutralizer to be skipped when attacker-controlled comment content containing a malicious [wpie_function] shortcode is substituted at runtime. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary PHP callables on the server. Exploitation requires an Administrator to perform the standard Export With Settings For Import followed by a New Import migration workflow, which is a routine operational task; the attacker themselves requires no account or authentication, needing only the ability to submit a pending comment on any comments-open post.

t: HCL BigFix MCM is vulnerable in Content Security Policy
d: Improper Content Security Policy (CSP) nonce implementation in HCL BigFix MCM allows a remote attacker to reduce the effectiveness of the Content Security Policy protection mechanism via an orphaned nonce value in the style-src directive of the CSP header without a corresponding nonce attribute on any <style> or <script> element.

t: CAPTCHA for Drupal 7 exposes login validation feedback after failed CAPTCHA
d: Observable Discrepancy vulnerability in Drupal CAPTCHA for Drupal 7 allows unauthenticated attackers to test login credentials despite CAPTCHA protection. When CAPTCHA is enabled on Drupal login forms, normal form validation can still run after a missing or incorrect CAPTCHA response. This may expose credential validation feedback and allow an attacker to distinguish invalid credentials from valid credentials paired with a failed CAPTCHA. This issue affects CAPTCHA for Drupal 7: from 7.x-1.0 through 7.x-1.7.

t: Drupal Icon API (Icon API: Menu) Stored XSS via unsanitized Title Wrapper Class
d: A stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability exists in the Icon API: Menu submodule of the Drupal 7 Icon API module. When a menu item is configured with the Title Wrapper option enabled, the value of the Title Wrapper Class field is output directly into an HTML attribute without sanitization or escaping. A user with the "administer menu icons" permission can inject a payload such as `title" onmouseover="alert(document.cookie)` that is rendered verbatim on every page displaying the affected menu item, executing arbitrary JavaScript in the browser of any user who interacts with the menu link. This can lead to session theft, account hijacking, and further attacks against site users. This issue affects Icon API 7.1.0.

t: probe-image-size before 7.5.0 Denial of Service via EXIF Sub-IFD Traversal
d: probe-image-size before 7.5.0 contains an algorithmic-complexity denial of service vulnerability in lib/exif_utils.js that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to exhaust CPU by supplying self-referencing EXIF IFDs. Attackers can submit a crafted 9.6 KB JPEG with repeated ExifIFD and InteropIFD pointers to block the Node.js event loop for about 23 seconds.

t: probe-image-size 7.4.0 ReDoS via SVG Doctype Prolog Parser
d: probe-image-size 7.4.0 contains a regular expression denial of service vulnerability in lib/common/svg_header.js that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to block the event loop via crafted SVG doctypes. Attackers can supply SVGs with an unclosed internal subset followed by many ']' characters to trigger quadratic backtracking in probe.sync, probe(stream) or probe(url), causing repeated event loop stalls.

t: probe-image-size before 7.5.0 Memory Exhaustion via AVIF Box Size
d: probe-image-size before 7.5.0 contains an unbounded memory allocation vulnerability in lib/parse_stream/avif.js that allows remote attackers to exhaust memory via attacker-declared ftyp or meta box sizes. Attackers can supply an AVIF stream or URL to probe(url) or probe(stream) declaring a huge box length, forcing the parser to buffer all received bytes and causing denial of service.

t: probe-image-size before 7.5.0 Memory Exhaustion via WebP EXIF Chunk Length
d: probe-image-size before 7.5.0 contains an unbounded memory buffering vulnerability in parseExif in lib/parse_stream/webp.js that allows remote attackers to exhaust memory via an attacker-declared EXIF chunk length. Attackers can supply a WebP stream or URL to probe(url) or probe(stream) declaring a huge EXIF length after VP8X, causing unbounded buffering and process memory exhaustion.

t: devpi-server before 6.21.0 Path Traversal via '..' User and Index Names
d: devpi-server before 6.21.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows authenticated users to write files outside the +files storage root by naming a user and index '..'. Attackers can self-register a '..' user, create a '..' index, and upload release files with attacker-chosen filenames and contents into a parent of the server directory.

t: devpi-web before 5.2.0 Unauthenticated Path Traversal via +doc Route
d: devpi-web before 5.2.0 contains an unauthenticated path traversal vulnerability in the +doc documentation route because docs_file_exists and docs_file_path in doczip.py never confine relpath to the documentation directory. Attackers can request a relpath with a leading // or percent-encoded .. segments to read server files, including the keyfs sqlite database holding password hashes.

t: Qwik City before 1.20.3 and Router before 2.0.0-rc.4 DoS via formToObj
d: Qwik City before 1.20.3 (@builder.io/qwik-city) and @qwik.dev/router before 2.0.0-rc.4 contain an improperly controlled object modification vulnerability in formToObj that allows unauthenticated attackers to overwrite built-in function properties. Attackers can send a form POST with nested field names traversing inherited members of string values, breaking Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call process-wide until server restart.

t: Cesanta Mongoose 7.22 before 7.24 Out-of-Bounds Read via mg_timegm
d: Cesanta Mongoose 7.22 before 7.24 with the built-in TLS stack contains an out-of-bounds read in mg_timegm() that allows remote attackers to crash the process via crafted X.509 certificate validity months. Attackers can present a certificate with month '00' or out-of-range values during the handshake, before signature verification, causing an unchecked dm array index and denial of service.

t: Cesanta Mongoose 7.21 before 7.24 Out-of-Bounds Read via IPv6 Checksum Validation
d: Cesanta Mongoose 7.21 before 7.24 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in rx_ip6() checksum validation that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to read past received packets by sending IPv6 extension headers. Attackers can send a single IPv6 TCP or ICMPv6 packet with extension headers, causing tcp6csum_ok() and icmp6csum_ok() to use the full payload length and read adjacent receive-buffer memory.

t: audio-separator before 0.47.2 RCE via Unsafe Pickle Deserialization of Demucs Models
d: audio-separator before 0.47.2 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability that allows attackers to execute code by supplying malicious Demucs .th model files loaded via torch.load with weights_only=False. Local users writing to the shared /tmp/audio-separator-models/ default directory, or attackers controlling unverified model download sources, can execute code when victims run Demucs separation.

t: highlight highlight.js Language Grammar livescript.js hljs.highlight redos
d: A flaw has been found in highlight highlight.js up to 11.12.0. The affected element is the function hljs.highlight of the file src/languages/livescript.js of the component Language Grammar Handler. Executing a manipulation of the argument text can lead to inefficient regular expression complexity. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. The pull request to fix this issue awaits acceptance.

t: OceanWP before 4.2.9 Stored XSS via EDD Category Name
d: OceanWP WordPress Theme before 4.2.9 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the oceanwp_edd_terms_list() function in inc/edd/edd-helpers.php, which allows authenticated users with EDD download category creation permissions to inject malicious JavaScript by crafting a category name that breaks out of an unescaped HTML title attribute. Attackers can create a category name containing an event-handler payload that executes in the browser of visitors who interact with the category link on the public EDD archive page, potentially compromising an administrator's session if they view the affected page while authenticated.

t: hankcs HanLP contextual_string_embedding.py RNNLanguageModel.load_language_model deserialization
d: A vulnerability has been found in hankcs HanLP up to 2.1.6. The affected element is the function RNNLanguageModel.load_language_model of the file hanlp/layers/embeddings/contextual_string_embedding.py. Such manipulation of the argument model_file leads to deserialization. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used. Upgrading to version 2.1.7 is sufficient to fix this issue. The name of the patch is 6962907e37dfa467fa6dee164b5b1d0a904b24db. The affected component should be upgraded.

t: hankcs HanLP TAR Archive Extraction io_util.py uncompress path traversal
d: A flaw has been found in hankcs HanLP up to 2.1.6. Impacted is the function uncompress of the file hanlp/utils/io_util.py of the component TAR Archive Extraction Handler. This manipulation causes path traversal. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. Upgrading to version 2.1.7 is recommended to address this issue. Patch name: feb0f82d12762cf4e687b9926efd90c672857780. You should upgrade the affected component.

t: continuedev continue Config Resolution LocalPlatformClient.ts LocalPlatformClient.resolveFQSNs information disclosure
d: A vulnerability has been found in continuedev continue up to 2.1.0. This vulnerability affects the function LocalPlatformClient.resolveFQSNs of the file core/config/yaml/LocalPlatformClient.ts of the component Config Resolution. Such manipulation of the argument Name leads to information disclosure. Local access is required to approach this attack. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.
